TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS GATE WERE WRONG and the record is worth keeping. The first
compared the looped network against loop 36's UNLOOPED tether and failed at 70%. The
second compared the modal plateau against <R^2> at a finite separation and failed by a
factor of 3 -- which turned out to be TWO errors compounding, neither of them the model:
<R^2> only tends to 2 G_ii once G_ij decays, and here G_ij/G_ii is still 0.76 at
n/3 separation, because the confinement correlation length is 302 bins = 7.5 Mb;
and the MSD had reached only 71% of its asymptote at the times sampled, since
the slowest mode has tau = 90,909.
BOTH ARE PHYSICAL FACTS ABOUT THIS CHROMOSOME, not bugs: chr21 is nowhere near its
asymptotic regime in space, and equilibrates slower than the times a cell spends in
interphase. They are outputs, and they are why the naive check could not work.
separately, and NOT a gate: the unlooped tether alone gives 301.5 b^2 against
125.4 looped, so cohesin compacts this chromosome 2.40-fold in mean
square, 1.55-fold in radius.

THE MODEL HAS A TIME AXIS AND IT IS CHEAP. Two clocks: relaxation inside a fixed loop set,
in closed form from the modes, and rewiring of the loop set itself from the KMC. The whole
dynamics cost 48s on four CPUs, because no trajectory is ever integrated.
AND IT REPRODUCES THE THING SINGLE-CELL HI-C FOUND: no individual configuration looks
like the map. TADs here are a property of the population, exactly as extrusion predicts.
